name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
o2_note: O2 not stated in our sources. BASS (2012) ran before N2 dilution was introduced (first used in BASS-II, NTRS 20210011385), so likely cabin air, but no value found. Pressure 1 atm from the BASS and BASS-II fabric paper (NTRS 20150008962).
flow_note: Kept 5-50 cm/s (matches the spaceflight101 BASS-II description). Sources differ: PSI-26 says airflow up to 40 cm/s, and a NASA BASS-II presentation (NTRS 20160000593) lists 0-55 cm/s as the main variable range. Recheck against the bass_sheet wording.
fuels: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass | Nomex | Ultem | PMMA | wax-saturated fiberglass | paraffin and Japan wax candles
geometry: Thin flat 12 x 1-2 cm; thick flat 5 x 1 cm x 1-2 mm; PMMA spheres 1-2 cm; candles 6 x 25 mm
measurements: video and still cameras | radiometer | anemometer | mass flow controller
variables: Material, thickness, shape, airflow speed, N2 suppressant flow
key_findings: Tests whether materials burn as well or better in microgravity when ventilation is adequate. | Best place to apply suppressant is harder to find in microgravity; badly placed suppressant can feed the flame by pulling in oxygen.
people: PI Paul Ferkul (NCSER); Sandra Olson (NASA GRC)

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
o2_note: PSI-25 BASS-II table, Calibrated initial O2 column: 13.6 to 22.2% across the tests (read from a screenshot, so allow +/-0.1). NASA papers (NTRS 20150008962, 20160000593) quote 16-21% for the fabric tests. Pressure 1 atm from NTRS 20150008962 (PSI-25 has no pressure column).
flow_note: PSI-25 'Air display' column: readings from 0 up to 49 (units not labelled, read as cm/s). PSI-26 description says airflow up to 40 cm/s and a NASA presentation (NTRS 20160000593) lists 0-55 cm/s. Recheck against the bass_sheet.
fuels: acrylic (PMMA) films and sheets | SIBAL | black and clear acrylic rods | acrylic sphere section
geometry: Thin flat 10 x 1-2 cm; rods; large sphere section
measurements: video and still cameras | radiometer | anemometer
variables: Ambient O2, airflow speed, fuel type and thickness, opposed vs concurrent flow
key_findings: Measured minimum O2 and flow needed for materials to burn in space and compared with Earth upward-burning limits. | Thin and thick fuel spread rates measured, plus a formula for the thin-to-thick transition. | Models predicted faster flame spread than observed, so models need improvement. | Data supports theoretical quenching boundaries.

name: BASS-Milliken (flame-retardant textiles)
o2_note: No BASS-M O2 or pressure values found yet. Uses the same MSG + SPICE hardware as BASS. Check the BASS-M PSI page.
flow_note: Same 5-50 cm/s as the BASS entries; not checked separately for BASS-M.
fuels: 10 flame-retardant treated textiles | untreated cotton controls
geometry: 44 textile samples with integrated igniter wires
measurements: video cameras | radiometer | anemometer
key_findings: Compares microgravity behaviour of flame-retardant fabrics with Earth behaviour; NASA screening uses upward-burning tests that ignore microgravity.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration I
o2_note: PSI Saffire-I sample table: S1 21.5-21.7% O2, S2 ~21.5% O2. Pressure 100 kPa (0.99 atm) from Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 2 (not in the PSI table).
flow_note: PSI Saffire-I sample table: 20 cm/s for both samples (S1 concurrent, S2 opposed).
hardware: Cygnus cargo vehicle after leaving ISS
measurements: cameras
key_findings: First large-scale fire in space; the previous largest space fire test was about index-card sized.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration II
o2_note: PSI Saffire-II table, samples 2-1 to 2-5 only (5 of 16 rows seen): ~21.5 to ~22.1% O2. Pressure 100 kPa (0.99 atm) from Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 2. Other 11 samples not yet checked.
flow_note: PSI Saffire-II samples 2-1 to 2-5: 20 cm/s. Upper value 25 cm/s from Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 2 (sample II-6).
hardware: Cygnus cargo vehicle after leaving ISS
fuels: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass | Nomex | acrylic (spacecraft window material)
measurements: cameras
key_findings: Widened the range of spacecraft materials burned at large scale.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration III
o2_note: O2 and pressure not in the PSI Saffire-III table. 21% O2 and 100 kPa (0.99 atm) from Urban et al., ICES-2021-266, Table 2 (sample III-1).
flow_note: Higher flow velocity than Saffire-I. PSI Saffire-III table: 30 cm/s for both samples (S1 concurrent, S2 opposed). ICES-2021-266 Table 2 lists 25 cm/s for III-1. The two sources disagree, so both are kept as the range.
hardware: Cygnus cargo vehicle after leaving ISS
measurements: cameras
key_findings: Repeated Saffire-I material at a higher airflow to see how ventilation changes large-scale fire growth.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration IV to VI
o2_note: Varied pressure and O2 toward exploration-vehicle atmospheres; values not stated. Not named in the challenge brief, check PSI for data. Values from Urban et al.: ICES-2021-266 Table 1 (Saffire IV 22.0% O2 and 100 kPa, Saffire V 25.4-26.2% O2 and 70.7-72.6 kPa) and ICES-2024-365 Table 1 (Saffire VI 28.8-31.0% O2 and 54.1-55.2 kPa). Pressure converted to atm (54.1 kPa = 0.53). Saffire VI covers only the three tests reported in that paper.
flow_note: Same two papers: 20 cm/s, reduced to 5 cm/s in some tests (IV-2, V-3, V-4, VI-3).
hardware: Cygnus cargo vehicle after leaving ISS
measurements: cameras | VI: fire detection, combustion product monitoring, post-fire cleanup
key_findings: Glowing char seen behind the flame front (IV). | V and VI target exploration spacecraft pressure and O2 ranges.

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
fuels: Teflon | Kapton | cellulose | silicone rubber | dibutyl phthalate on wick
measurements: particle size and count detectors | ionization and photoelectric smoke detectors
variables: Airflow rate, heating temperature, smoke aging time
key_findings: Much of the smoke mass is in particles larger than 1 micron; Teflon smoke is mostly under 1 micron. | Mean particle diameters were 100 to 200 nm. | Aging cuts particle count a lot while mass stays steady (coagulation). | Detectors need to cover a wide size range; early detection should target pyrolysis products, not soot.
people: PI David Urban (NASA GRC); NIST collaborators

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Reflight
fuels: Teflon | Kapton | cotton | silicone rubber | Pyrell
measurements: thermal precipitator for TEM | aerosol instruments | commercial, ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors
key_findings: Compared flight and ground results and tested the real ISS and Shuttle detectors. | Shuttle detectors were ionization-based; ISS detectors use near-IR scattering and are most sensitive above 1 micron, so each misses part of the size range.

name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT and DAFT-2)
measurements: modified P-Trak
key_findings: Confirmed the modified P-Trak works in microgravity before it was used for smoke in SAME. | Useful for telling dust from smoke, which matters for false alarms (lunar dust).

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
measurements: burning rate | extinction | flame radiation | soot concentration | soot temperature
variables: O2 level, suppressant type and amount, pressure, fuel, droplet size
key_findings: Measured how well CO2 and He suppress flames in microgravity and estimated the limiting oxygen index. | Low-pressure suppression data supports strategies like isolating a module and venting the cabin. | Cool flames were first seen in ISS droplet tests in 2012 (per ACME sheet).

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
flow_note: Sub-buoyant convective flow by moving a tethered droplet; speed not stated.
fuels: pure fuels | bi-component and surrogate mixtures | bio-derived surrogates (FLEX-ICE-GA)
geometry: Droplets 2-4 mm; tethered moving droplets; 2-droplet arrays
measurements: burning rate | flame spread along droplet arrays (FLEX-2J)
variables: Fuel mixture, convective flow, droplet spacing
key_findings: Extends droplet burning to practical fuels, moving droplets and droplet-to-droplet flame spread.
people: Lead PI Forman Williams (UCSD); JAXA and ASI partners

name: Cool Flames Investigation
todo: Fill from PSI page: fuels, O2, pressure.
key_findings: Follows up the 2012 ISS discovery of cool flames around droplets, which burn at low temperature and are hard to see.

name: ACME Burning Rate Emulator
fuels: gaseous fuels emulating paper, plastic and alcohol
geometry: Flat porous burner with heat flux sensors and surface thermocouple
measurements: heat flux | surface temperature | ACME imaging and pyrometry
key_findings: Only ACME experiment aimed at fire prevention; tests material flammability in still air and checks flammability test methods for low and partial gravity.

name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
o2_note: Highest O2 in PSI microgravity tests: O2/N2 up to 85% O2 flowed from the burner into a fuel/N2 chamber (brief).
fuels: propane and other gases in the chamber
measurements: ACME imaging and diagnostics
key_findings: Only microgravity data at very high oxygen, so the closest match for oxygen-rich habitats and suits.

name: ACME Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
measurements: imaging | pyrometry | soot volume fraction
key_findings: Sooty microgravity flames are taller, wider and cooler, with 5 to 8 times more soot than on Earth. | Diluted microgravity flames are more stable and lift off at lower fuel levels.

name: ACME Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
geometry: Insulated burner with mesh electrode 35-50 mm away, up to 10 kV
measurements: ion current | flame response time
key_findings: Electric field acts on flame ions to mimic partial gravity, the only PSI proxy for Moon/Mars gravity.

name: ACME Flame Design
measurements: soot inception and extinction limits
key_findings: Flammability and soot limits under oxygen enrichment.

name: ACME Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
measurements: radiative and convective extinction limits | pulsating instabilities
key_findings: Extinction behaviour of sooty and soot-free flames in still air.

name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
geometry: Small gas jets (lighter-sized), several nozzle diameters
measurements: flame shape imaging | stabilisation height | temperature field | smoke point
key_findings: Soot controls radiant heat from fires, so smoke point data improves heat release predictions for spacecraft fires. | Could support performance-based material selection.
people: PI David Urban (NASA GRC); Peter Sunderland (UMD)

name: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
measurements: still images | video
variables: Fuel, dilution, nozzle diameter, coflow speed
key_findings: Flame attachment and liftoff limits as air speed rises; precursor to ACME CLD.
